original_test_intent: Verify one physical SUT power-button press triggers an orderly OS shutdown and the host subsequently powers on, boots and logs in cleanly without OS/BMC errors.
original_method: A qualified operator performs the exact button press and later power-on while the agent captures ACPI, service, filesystem, power-transition, boot, health and log evidence.
manual_activity: User approves ACPI/workload/recovery plan; qualified operator presses the physical button once, confirms off state, powers on and validates console login.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC identity and installed OS/kernel/firmware
Power-button/ACPI action, shutdown timeout and off-state definition
Active service/job quiescence and maintenance plan
Qualified operator, front-panel/KVM/OOB access and evidence storage
safety_requirements: Confirm ACPI action is graceful rather than forced power-off
Quiesce critical work and verify filesystem/RAID health
Continuously observe KVM/BMC and service/unmount progress
Stop on timeout, hang/panic/BSOD, storage/boot/power/BMC fault or recovery loss
Do not issue a second button press, forced power cycle or automatic repair
agent_execution_scope: Capture pre-state workload, mounts, RAID, health, ACPI and logs
Record button timestamp, shutdown/service/unmount and BMC transition evidence
Collect post-power-on boot/login/storage/health and error logs
Do not press hardware, substitute software shutdown, power-cycle automatically or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve ACPI policy, safe window and recovery
Provide qualified operator and own physical/boot recovery
Review orderly shutdown and clean boot evidence to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: shutdown -h now tests an OS command path, not the required physical power-button ACPI event; BMC power state cannot prove orderly service/filesystem shutdown.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use read-only OS/BMC collectors synchronized with the operator's single physical press, off-state observation and later approved power-on/login.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Installed OS/login, physical button, orderly shutdown, power-on/boot/login, log review and source 5/5 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correlate the physical event with ACPI log receipt, service stop, filesystem unmount, BMC power state and a clean subsequent boot ID/login.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds traceable state transitions and recovery gates without replacing the button stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Evidence collection is automated; physical press/off confirmation/power-on remain manual.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some firmware interprets a long or repeated press as hard-off, so operator timing must be defined.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must define button duration, ACPI action and maximum shutdown timeout; SSH or BMC shutdown commands are not equivalent unless a separate variant is approved.
expected_evidence: Approval, ACPI policy and exact SUT/BMC identity
Operator/button timestamp and ACPI event receipt
Service stop, filesystem unmount and BMC power transition/off evidence
Complete OS/BMC/SEL event triage, recovery readiness and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require a physical power-button graceful shutdown followed by power-on and clean boot; software shutdown is merely a rejected review substitution.

blocked_analysis.analysis: ACPI policy, operator, maintenance and recovery are supplyable prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Restores the physical ACPI path and replaces a power-status-only shortcut with end-to-end service/filesystem/off/boot evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC showing power off cannot distinguish orderly shutdown from sudden power loss, and an SSH shutdown bypasses the power-button event handler entirely. The test therefore needs correlated ACPI receipt, shutdown journal/service and unmount completion before the power transition, followed by a new clean boot/login and storage-health check.
